dedupe_keys.name: cerf capacity expansion regional feasibility model

description: Pacific Northwest National Laboratory publishes CERF to evaluate where future electricity-generation capacity can be placed. The Python model takes regional, yearly technology-expansion targets from a parent model such as GCAM and allocates plants to feasible 1 km grid cells. Technologies compete for cells using net locational cost, combining interconnection costs with operational value. Suitability rasters and exclusion buffers constrain placement, and previous placements can carry into later years until retirement. Source and pip packages are free under BSD-2-Clause; results are returned as a dataframe or CSV with plant attributes. The model supports capacity-planning simulations. The supplied application covers the conterminous United States and can use data-gridcerf. A caveat is that the method represents screening-scale siting and costs, not detailed permitting, power flow or construction feasibility. The current README specifies Python 3.10 or newer and separate sample-data installation. No package data were downloaded and no siting run was executed.
